title: BetOnMe (HackKU26 MLH Winner)
summary: Decentralized self-accountability platform using XRP Ledger escrows to route failed stakes to charity, backed by EXIF/GPS proof verification and Gemini Vision.
problem: Traditional self-accountability apps rely on centralized trust or weak honor systems, making it difficult to enforce financial stakes without risking user fund custody.
approach: I engineered a non-custodial XRPL escrow pipeline combined with Gemini Vision API and EXIF/GPS metadata parsing to verify proof photos and automatically route forfeited funds directly to charity.
outcome: Won MLH's Best Use of Solana prize at HackKU26 and received a Ledger Nano S Plus. Although BetOnMe was built on XRP Ledger rather than Solana, MLH judges selected it because its non-custodial escrow design fit the challenge's intent.
designChoices: Non-Custodial XRPL Escrows: Implemented native EscrowCreate, EscrowFinish, and EscrowCancel primitives targeting charity wallet addresses directly so the platform never holds user funds.
Automated Proof Pipeline: Integrated Gemini Vision API with custom EXIF/GPS metadata parsers featuring hemisphere-aware coordinate fixes and timestamp fallbacks.
Lazy On-Chain Settlement: Designed an on-demand resolution flow executed during app load to finalize past-due bets without background worker crons.
Multi-Week Recurring Contracts: Structured pooled-stake escrows covering multi-session commitments where a single missed check-in forfeits the pool to charity.
